lookForward.fits: Fat Bear Week champion crowned today, 29 September 2026.
lookForward.headline: Fat Bear Week champion crowned today
lookForward.line: The final vote at fatbearweek.org closes this evening and Katmai National Park names its fattest brown bear of 2026. The winner gets nothing and needs nothing. It has a den to get to.

source.name: National Park Service: Fat Bear Week 2026

more: Katmai National Park is on the Alaska Peninsula, a place with more brown bears than people. In late summer the bears stand in the Brooks River and catch sockeye salmon as the fish leap the falls, eating as much as they can before winter. A bear that goes into its den in October will not eat again until spring, so the fatter, the better.

Fat Bear Week turns that into a game. The park picks twelve or so bears, shows a photo of each from July and one from September, and pairs them in a knockout bracket. Anyone can vote once a day at fatbearweek.org, free, no account needed. Voting runs from Tuesday 22 September to Tuesday 29 September 2026, when the champion is named. Nobody tells the bear.
The live cameras at explore.org show the Brooks Falls all day. Watch for a while; it is very calming, and the salmon are still running.

funFact.statement: A Katmai bear can lose a third of its weight in hibernation.
funFact.reveal: Five months without food or water, living on fat. In at a thousand pounds, out at seven hundred. The fatter, the safer.

kindness.fits: Tuesday; a bear wins for being well fed.
kindness.text: Feed someone today. Bring lunch for a colleague, or cook for the person who usually cooks.

joke.setup: What did the Fat Bear champion say in its acceptance speech?
joke.punchline: Nothing. It was asleep by November.

riddle.riddle: The rounder I am, the more likely I am to see spring. What am I?
